rule: Retain a historical shape only when it carries a current domain capability or a required extension boundary; remove compatibility-only identity and keep advanced retained shapes out of the preferred path.

entries.rationale: Send, publish, request/response, consumer, retry, redelivery, fault, outbox, saga, state machine, routing slip, and MessageData are industry messaging concepts rather than framework identity. Renaming them would add proprietary vocabulary without removing complexity.
IConsumer<T> is the minimal strongly typed application delivery contract and is the preferred consumer model.

The definition model still carries custom endpoint-definition and provider-extension capability, but ordinary retry and concurrency configuration is now performed in AddConsumer<T> and the type is hidden from default IntelliSense.
The wrapper preserves compile-time MultiBus DI ownership for internal resolution; it is not an application abstraction and is hidden from default IntelliSense.
Manual construction remains a capability for non-container hosts and provider authors; applications register and inject IMessageScheduler, and the factory family is hidden from default IntelliSense.
Destination-addressed sending and publishing are first-class application capabilities, not compatibility aliases.

Composable middleware and provider integration require a public extension protocol. Preferred application journeys expose only focused callbacks and never ask developers to construct pipeline internals.
A stable byte envelope is required between persistence stores and transport dispatchers, while applications use typed IDurableSender<TBus>.SendAsync.
Request-client construction retains transport and scope lifecycle capability; applications consume IRequestClient<T> through dependency injection.
No former package, namespace, assembly identity, or source identifier remains in production or preferred sample artifacts.
Historical test-framework carriers were retired only after their obligations were mapped to native executing tests.
Compatibility-only verification paths were retired after capability-by-capability replacement, leaving one native release verdict.
